about: Every dimension the Ford build uses, with its source (an id in references.json), where in it, and the text it stands on (quote), which sources.py finds in the fetched copy. Values are in the source's own units; the build converts (1 ft = 0.3048 m). Where sources disagree, every value is recorded, with the one the model uses and why. Positions no source states are measured from the imagery and photos and go in layout, each saying what it was fitted to.

length.use: neither: the deck plan is measured off noaa2022, and the length follows
length.note: 1,092 ft is also the Nimitz's figure in the same tables. The orthos measure the flight deck at about 331-334 m, which fits 1,092 ft (332.8 m); what the 1,106 ft figure measures is not stated.

waterline.note: relays the Naval Vessel Register's withdrawn field; the same as the Nimitz's

deck.also: airlant ("Flight Deck Width : 256 feet"); globalsecurity ("Extreme Beam 256 ft")

navigational.note: its metric 7.8 m is wrong: 39 ft is 11.9 m. Decision 23: the model floats at her deployed load, read from the draught marks in deployed photos and checked against this.

area.use: a check only: the planform measured off noaa2022 gives its own area
area.note: the totals disagree; each puts the Ford about 2-10% above the Nimitz.

form.quote: same hull form as the CVN 68 Nimitz class
form.also: dote2019 ("same hull form as the CVN 68 Nimitz-class"); crs ("uses the basic Nimitz-class hull form")
form.note: no public lines, offsets or tank reports for CVN-68/77/78: the underwater hull is shaped from the 2013 dry-dock photos, at 1 m (decision 10)

deployed.where: stem draught marks, at the waterline
deployed.method: the waterline lies 0.25-0.35 ft below the foot of the 38 (95 px per foot in a 2x crop of x 900-1400, y 4650-5200); the 8's reflection fixes the water
deployed.note: forward draught only: no stern marks have been read, so the trim is unknown. A second deployed reading, DVIDS 9628694 (Souda Bay, 22-23 Feb 2026), gives about 37 ft 7 in; the homecoming of 16 May 2026 (DVIDS 9688116) about 34 ft, extrapolated past fouled numerals, at the end of a deployment. Decision 23 floats the model at the deployed draught; the navigational maximum is 39 ft (overall.draught.navigational).

boot.where: stem, top edge of the black boot-topping
boot.method: 0.8 ft above the foot of the 41 numeral in the same crop
boot.note: where the black waterline band meets the grey at the stem (decision 17)

length.quote: 60 feet long at the flight deck base

height.note: above the flight deck; whether this includes the mast is not stated

placement.quote: 140 feet further aft and 3 feet further outboard than previous carriers
placement.note: relative to an unnamed earlier carrier, so the island is placed from the imagery; this is a check

taller.quote: stands 20 feet taller than islands on previous aircraft carriers

length.quote: It measures 85 feet long and 52 feet wide
length.note: one starboard elevator, "the third and final aircraft elevator" installed (its image is named Ford_Elevator_1): elevator 1, which measures 26.0-26.4 m along its outboard side. Elevator 2 measures 27.05 m and elevator 3 25.89 m (references/research/deck).

width.quote: It measures 85 feet long and 52 feet wide
width.note: one starboard elevator, "the third and final aircraft elevator" installed (its image is named Ford_Elevator_1): elevator 1, which measures 26.0-26.4 m along its outboard side. Elevator 2 measures 27.05 m and elevator 3 25.89 m (references/research/deck).

measured.where: layout.elevators: elevator 1's outline off noaa2022, its inboard corner 0.03 m across in dvids7694421, its outboard edge the orthophoto's (references/research/deck, match)

width.use: measured: the platform meets the deck opening the photos see. 52 ft (15.85 m) is 0.52 m less, more than its rounding (0.15 m) or the imagery's fit (0.1-0.6 m on one side) explains; what the published figure measures (the platform inside its edge fittings, say) is not stated.

elevators.note: where each sits is measured off the imagery: two to starboard forward of the island and one to port (pms378 slide 3's top view; noaa2022).

engines.value: four engines and three wires, as CVN 76 and CVN 77
engines.quote: consisting of four engines and three wires
engines.note: the planned positions were similar to CVN 76's and 77's; the fourth engine was never fitted. The wires' positions are measured from the photos (decision 10: 0.1 m)

target.quote: aiming for the number 2 wire is standard operating procedure
target.note: said of CVN 77, whose layout the Ford's follows (dote2025: three wires, as CVN 76 and 77). Where the lens puts the hook on a 3-wire deck is not public; the 2001 LSO NATOPS gives only the 4-wire rule (halfway between the 2 and 3).

runout.quote: Length of deck pendant runout 344 ft (to tail hook)
runout.note: the Mk 7 Mod 3's: the Advanced Arresting Gear's run-out is not public. The flight core stops a trap in this run-out, closed loop to it whatever the weight, speed or thrust, as the gear's controller is (decision 24).

force.quote: Produce a sustained launch force of ~1.3 MN
force.note: the flight core's catapult pulls no more than this

profile.quote: the EMALS is capable of operating within the 1.05 max peak-to-mean acceleration requirement
profile.note: the flight core's catapult is closed loop to the end speed set for the jet, at a constant acceleration once its force has risen (decision 24)

speed.quote: Achieve launch speeds of up to ~100 m/s
speed.note: the end speed the flight core caps a shot at (the ship file's catapults' speed)

catapults.note: two on the bow and two in the waist; their tracks are measured off noaa2022.

lens.note: the shore-training layout's lens face from the ramp lights: a check on the Ford's lens position, not her own value

centreline.quote: The deck centerline markings shall consist of a 3-foot-wide stripe symmetrical about the deck centerline with alternating yellow and white sections
centreline.note: the shore-training form; the Ford's own is measured off noaa2022, which shows the same pattern

sections.quote: The sections shall be 45 feet long beginning with a yellow section
sections.note: the shore-training form; the Ford's own is measured off noaa2022, which shows the same pattern

outer.quote: The outer edge stripes shall be one-foot wide with the outer edge 40 feet from the deck centerline
outer.note: the shore-training form; the Ford's own is measured off noaa2022, which shows the same pattern

inner.quote: The inner edge stripes shall be 3 feet wide with the inner edges 28 feet from the deck centerline
inner.note: the shore-training form; the Ford's own is measured off noaa2022, which shows the same pattern

bars.quote: The two edge stripes shall be connected at 75-foot intervals by 10-foot-wide white bars
bars.note: the shore-training form; the Ford's own is measured off noaa2022, which shows the same pattern

ramp.quote: The ramp athwartship marking is a 10-foot-wide white stripe across the ramp end of the deck
ramp.note: the shore-training form; the Ford's own is measured off noaa2022, which shows the same pattern

colours.value: white, the centreline's sections alternately yellow
colours.quote: The markings shall be non-retroreflective white except for the sections of the centerline markings which are non-retroreflective yellow
colours.note: the paint's colours on the Ford are measured from her photos

markings.note: the Ford's own landing-area markings are measured off noaa2022; navair5150 WP 006 04 gives the shore-training form to compare.

tacan.note: chapter 3: ships' identifiers are two letters. The channel is set per operation and is not public.

layout.about: Placements no source states, in the contract frame (x forward, y up, z starboard, metres; origin on the centreline at the deployed waterline, midway between the flight deck's aft and forward extremes). The deck plan is measured on the orthophotos noaa2022 (primary), noaa2018 and VBMP 2025, each corrected for relief and the grid's scale; their frame F (origin where the centreline meets the stern edge) gives x = F - 165.8585. Each entry says what it was measured on; provisional ones wait for the photo match (stage 5).

notes.deck: height: 18.27 m above the deployed waterline (spread 0.23 m), the raised elevators' top edges against the boot top in three starboard beams (dvids9167788, dvids9142613, dvids7473567) through cameras solved on the deck plan; 18.66 at the starboard bow corner (research/hull). thickness: the edge plate's depth, not measured. outline: 29 corners and joins of robust line fits to the deck edges (noaa2022; 0.1-0.6 m, 1.5-1.9 m at the port bow's transition), the elevators' platforms left out. The starboard quarter's notch: both stern photos (dvids7107228, dvids7107229) show the deck stepping down to a lower platform aft of x -151; its inboard forward corner is the photo match's (-150.8, 22.25), 0.24 m from two photos (research/match), not the orthophoto's (-151.8, 17.0). texture: about 4.1 cm a texel, square texels.
notes.fittings: shuttle: a 1.25 x 0.65 m footprint (±0.2) from catapult 3's at battery in dvids7694421, its top 0.47 of its base's width (dvids9478858, kennedy10011978); its height not measured. deflector: 6 modules across, raised 50 ± 3° (its top 3.4-3.7 m above the deck: the Ford's dvids9455182 and Kennedy's photos, against each deflector's flush depth); its thickness not measured. sheave, support, stanchion: see landing. console: the integrated catapult control stations (references/research/iccs): the bow's in the deck between catapults 1 and 2, its lid an elongated hexagon 3.32 x 2.35 m, and the waist's at the port deck edge abeam the waist's 6, its lid a trapezoid 4.31 m outboard and 1.67 m inboard by 1.66, in a well outboard of the edge; each rises out of its surface while its catapults are manned, the bow's 0.7 m (0.6 and 0.8 in two photos), the waist's 0.65 (+-0.2, scaled); the bow's band right outside its lid's rim on every side. antenna: the whips' radius provisional. sheave colour: the tops 1.27-1.53 times the white stripes' in linear light in dvids9478807 (side on, the deck beside it) and 1.5-1.7 times a painted white ring in commons220325-CO784-2240 (overhead): a clean near-white, brighter than the worn stripes (the user, 2026-11-04, from the photo: small white circles); the red triangle on the side facing the wire left out.
notes.elevators: outline: robust line fits to each platform's four sides (noaa2022; elevator 3's inboard side noaa2018), about 0.1-0.6 m; trapezoids, wider at the deck edge. thickness and travel are not measured, and nothing drives the elevators yet (decision 14). Elevator 2's outboard side: 27.05 ± 0.15 m between its half-level ends on noaa2022 (and 27.0 in the photo match), not 85 ft; hiielevator's 85 x 52 ft is one starboard elevator, which elevator 1 (26.0-26.4 m) matches.
notes.catapults: track: the track's centre traced every metre (noaa2018 band, noaa2022 rails), its ends where the track's signature falls to half (noaa2018, 0.5 m; catapult 3's forward end 1.5 m). battery: 1 m forward of the track's aft end, and stroke: the track less battery and 6 m of braking, inside the 94-103 m the sources give (decision 24): both provisional. deflector: its four sides fitted lowered (noaa2018, outside the 2022-2026 era; VBMP 2025 differs by up to 0.8 m); hinge is its forward edge, square to the ship, not to the track.
notes.landing: line: the painted centreline's centre (noaa2022, rms 0.07 m over 415 profiles); angle positive to port. ramp: the ramp stripe's forward edge on the centreline. wires: where each pendant runs, between its pair of round deck sheaves (references/research/deck: noaa2022 housing centres to 0.12 m, the pendants rigged and cast through commons220325-CO784-2240's camera at 7 px, the painted dash pairs 0.32-0.39 m aft); x along the line from the ramp, ±0.15 m; 54.14, 66.38 and 79.22, 2.7-2.9 m aft of the first reading, which took the barricade's row of deck fittings for wire 3. ends: where each pendant leaves its sheave, on the sheave's inboard side at mid-height (dvids9455182), ±0.2 m. sheaves: the round housings, 1.0 m across and 0.16 m proud raised, a fourth pair at u 81.17 for the barricade. supports: four leaf-spring bows under each pendant at about ±4.2 and ±9.6 m across the line (±0.35 m), 1.45 m between their pads, their crown not measured (the Mk 7 manual's 2-5.5 in). barricade: flush stanchion trays outboard of the fourth sheave pair, each hinged at its head; port from commons220325 and noaa2022 (±0.5 m), starboard from noaa2022 alone (±0.7 m); raised heights not measured.
notes.paint: measured: see deckwear (the stripes' shares in two unclipped photos)
notes.markings: Measured on noaa2022 in the landing frame: the centreline, the edge stripes' centres and the cross bars' places; widths from the shore standard (markings), which the stripes' measured spacing matches to 3 cm. The centreline's sections: 13.69 m measured (45 ft), yellow from u -6.5 every 27.38 m. The ramp stripe runs from the port deck edge to the starboard outer stripe. Each wire's pair of dashes, 1.8 x 0.5 m, 6.1 m either side of the centreline (noaa2022 and VBMP 2025). The bow's 78 traced on the 4 cm noaa2022 view. Not yet: the foul lines (none seen), the taxi lines, the elevators' edges.
notes.hull: Measured from the photos through cameras solved on the deck plan (research/hull: report.md, hull.json's evidence, the overlays). stem: the level starboard beam's silhouette, 13.1 m aft of the deck's bow tip on the waterline (x 153.0); transom: x -163.0, its bottom y -1.1, its outline cast from dvids7107228; waterline 316.0 m. stations: the waterplane's half-breadth from the boot top seen from above (two photos, the middle body calibrated to the cited beam), below it superellipse sections to a flat keel at the deployed draught (assumed: no photo shows them); forward of x 105 the flare to the deck is assumed. knuckle: the top of the sunlit hull side in the level starboard beam (0.2 m), carried forward of the sponsons at the gallery's foot; the port side mirrors starboard, unmeasured. gallery: the deck-edge band's depth, starboard (0.1-0.2 m); port copies it, unmeasured. bulb: its heights and width from the 2013 dry-dock photo; its length and nose (x 157) assumed. screws: four of 21 ft (6.4 m; Huntington Ingalls, 3 October 2013, "At 21 feet in diameter", five blades in DVIDS 1034894); lateral, each pair's offset from the centreline, inboard then outboard, is an estimate: no public photo shows the stern gear where a camera can be solved (references/research/sides).
notes.island: Measured from the photos (research/island: report.md, island.json's evidence, the overlays): a bundle of six photos' cameras on the deck plan's anchors (astern, ahead and near-nadir strong, 3.5-5.9 px), 15 triangulated points (domes, yardarm tips, the pole; 0.13-0.45 m) and 75 silhouette pixels cast onto planes another view fixes (cross-checks 0.2-0.5 m). Base 18.60 x 9.35 m at x -101.45 to -82.85, z 24.05 to 33.40; roof 21.5-22.5 m above the deck; pole top 45.3 m. About 1 m: the aft platforms' z extents, the mast house's width, the mast's x (0.5-1.3 m), the upper block's inboard step. Not modelled: the trunk's small platforms, whips, railings.
notes.lens: measured (references/research/lights: report.md, results.json, the overlays): a bundle of dvids9478807's camera with the r15 cameras of dvids7107228 and dvids7694421 held fixed, the lamps cast onto the lens face. position: the cell column's centre at datum height, ±(0.4, 0.15, 0.15) m, 508 ft along the landing line from the ramp against the shore replica's 410-430 ft (navair5150); x rests on one overhead mark. facing: 10.8° from dead aft, square to the landing line within its 4°. lights: 10 green datum lights a side 0.189 m apart, 3 red wave-off a side 0.29 m above and below the datum, 2 cut a side 0.54 m above; spacings to 0.01-0.02 m, scale to 3%. cells: 12 at 0.165 m centred on the datum (8 seen), a ball travel of ±0.99 m.
notes.lights: measured: drop, flood, masthead, obstruction; placed by rule, not seen: centreline, edge, elevator, forward, outline, ramp (references/research/lights). centreline, edge, ramp, forward: navair5150 WP 006 04's shore replica of the landing area's lights (18 centreline at 45 ft, edge rows 35 ft either side, 12 ramp, 10 forward), laid on layout.landing and clipped to the deck and the painted stripes, which match that replica within 3 cm. drop: the yellow bar down the stern in dvids7107228, 8 even points for lamps not resolved, its colour never seen lit. flood, masthead, obstruction: dvids9344251 at dusk through a camera on the island's points, ±0.3 m in y and z and 1 m in x; the floods show green. outline: blue lights along the deck edge in dvids9478938, placed every 18 m along the outline. elevator: no Ford evidence, every 6 m along each platform's outboard edge. Side and stern lights: not seen lit in any 2022-2026 photo.
notes.antennas: port_aft and port_forward: whips lowered aft and outboard at 28-38° off the ship's axis in noaa2022 (and one at sea in dvids9411247); length: the 4.2-4.3 m seen beyond the deck-edge structures, the whole not measured; base ±0.6 m. starboard_forward: the tall mast raised beside the bow console during launches (dvids7456172), 12.8 ± 1.5 m (its noaa2022 shadow and that photo), base ±1 m; never seen lowered, so it is built fixed. starboard_forward's base moved 2.0 m forward of the orthophoto shadow's reading (69.8, ±1 m): the sky check puts it 1.9 m aft in dvids9167788 and about 3 m in dvids9142613 (references/research/sky).
notes.parking: where the parked start's nose wheel stands (#133), heading positive to port: aft of the island on the starboard side, placed rather than measured. With the wings folded (8.6 m) the jet's footprint (z 10.2-18.8) lies 1 m inboard of the island's bridge wing (z 19.8) so it taxis forward past the island, 18 m aft of its aft face (x -101.45), and just inside the landing area's starboard foul line (about z 11.4 there), as a jet waiting to taxi stands.
notes.sides: Measured from the photos through the photo match's cameras and the level beam's re-solved one (references/research/sides: results.json, the overlays). sponsons: plans ±0.3-0.5 m from the overhead and one oblique view, top and bottom ±0.2-1.0. weapons: positions and heights measured; their shapes simple boxes, pedestals and radomes, since no source here gives their dimensions (the Mk 15's 4.7 m from a secondary site). A third Phalanx on a port sponson amidships is seen only from overhead and left out. domes_edge: SATCOM-size domes on small deck-edge sponsons, overhead only. catwalks: plans from the overhead, floors inferred from the racks hung on them (±0.6-0.8). racks: two tiers of raft canisters, x ±0.5. openings: the hangar openings under the elevators (port ±1.5 m, one weak camera) and the transom's two bays. island: windows (glass) and the Dual Band Radar's faces (panel, 10-20% darker and bluer than the grey), each from one to three views. Not built: the boat bays and recesses (on structure the hull loft lacks), the anchors, the bow's chocks; the island's 78 and the stem's draught marks wait for the lettering texture. There is no 78 on the bow and no name on the transom in 2022-2026.
notes.lettering: the island's two 78s, white with a thin dark outline (references/research/sides, lettering): starboard on the face at z 33.4, its corners from three photos (±0.3 along, ±0.2 up); port on the base's face at z 24.05, 5.0 m wide (±0.5). The port pair measured y 21.0-26.0 from its 2017 photo and 20.1-25.4 from its 2022 one; the first would put its top 0.53 m inside the second level's overhang (its bottom at y 25.47), so it is set 4.85 m tall as the starboard pair is, its top at 25.4. Drawn by letters.py in DejaVu Sans Bold stretched to the measured boxes, on the haze grey (the build's grey in sRGB). The stem's draught marks (draught): numerals 6 in high (0.152 m, the facts entry) with their feet at whole feet of draught, 38 to 41 ft over the deployed waterline's 37.7, on both sides; measured at x 154.0 ±1.0, they stand 0.6 m aft of the measured stem at their height (153.8-153.9), white on the boot's black. The bulbous-bow star is left out: measured about 2 m forward of the numerals, it would fall ahead of the stem. There is no 78 on the bow and no name on the transom in 2022-2026.
notes.stern: references/research/stern: the photo match re-run with 40 stern marks and dvids7694418 added, every stern mark within 5 px (0.1-0.3 m), points solved ±0.2-0.37 m. sponsons port_aft, starboard_aft: plans and heights from the solved corners, their tops and bottoms sloping as measured (the starboard bottom falls 0.9 m outboard, two cameras within 1 px); the aft faces slant, the inboard ends from the overhead (±0.4). port_gun_tub, starboard_gun_tub: railed tubs on the outboard faces, built solid to their rails (±0.4); their brackets and guns not built. fantail: corrected to x -170..-164.1, z 11..18.3, y 6.2..6.9; its Phalanx stands on it. wedges.transom_port_flare: the transom's diagonal below the port sponson, a metre deep (how far forward it runs is not seen); the starboard one, an astern cast only, not built. hull.quarters: the walls forward of the sponsons, vertical from their feet to the deck's underside, the deck overhanging them: port at z -33.35..-33.2 to x -118.7 (fitted by eye in two views, its forward end in one, ±1.5); starboard provisional, at the sponson's 36.65 to x -135 (its foot seen at 9.3-9.4 in two views, its z in none). The Mk 29 and RAM bases are the sponsons' new tops under their measured tops.
notes.bow: references/research/bow: the photo match's cameras re-solved with the bow's own points free (dvids9688116 and dvids3299641 added, 3.2-7 px). stem: y 0-7 from three side views relative to the face's lower corner (±0.5-0.6), the face's centreline above, the deck-edge band's front at 166.2; below y 0 the build's (under water in every photo). face: one flat plate on x = 146.38 + 1.294 y, its creases straight from (156.21, 7.62, ±2.02) to (166.23, 15.48, ±12.81) (±0.3-0.5); the loft runs each height straight from the last station to the crease, so the sections ahead of x 156.2 take the face as their flat bottom. stations 150 and 145: the flare from the anchor crowns (y 8.6) and the oval chocks (y 13.25) up (±0.6-0.8), the build's below; 145 and 135 held at least as full as the station ahead above y 8.6, so the bow never widens going forward (fitted, not measured). The flare between the creases and the deck edge is not measured. The waterplane forward of x 105 is not measured; the built one lies inside both tangent bounds. The bullnose ring's height on the face (13.01, ±0.25) is measured; it is on the centreline.
notes.sides2: references/research/sides2: the photo match with the 2022 port view (commons221126-QI061-2036R) added at 5.6 px, the overhead rectified at the catwalks' height. hull.knuckle port: level at 4.6 (4.48-4.74, ±0.2) from x -81 to 59 in the 2022 view; the steps it had are the starboard elevators' fairings (the level beam shows them, rounded at each end), which the port copy carried. The starboard's dips at x 37-42, -18.4 and 97-102 lie under overhangs whose shadows the lit edge followed: levelled, and rising steadily to the bow. The bow's knuckle at 7.9 (±0.2) from x 110 to 156 (2022 and 2019 port views; starboard its mirror). hull.gallery port: the band's foot at 14.46 and 14.56 where the angled deck's creases meet it (±0.3), carried along the diagonal from deck corner 15. hull.flare port: the flat facet under the diagonal (T1, K1, V, T2, 49.5° from vertical) and the two triangles behind it (V, T2, K2; K1, V, K2), from one view checked by eye in a second; K1 and K2 re-cast onto the hull (±0.4-0.6), V onto the facet's plane. hull.walls: the quarters' walls as before, and the vertical wall under the port deck edge from x -15 to 20.7 down to 12.2 (±0.3; its z assumed at the deck edge). Not measured: the starboard facets, port aft of x -57, the bow's lower facet. hull.antifouling: the black-to-red edge at -2.8 (±0.3) in the 2013 dry dock (16 columns at x 54-135); its colour the red's ratio to the haze grey in shade there, less the flare the black shows against the sunlit black (souda2023), on the build's grey. racks: canisters 1.5 x 0.8 m lying fore and aft, two tiers (16.3-17.2, 17.3-18.3, ±0.3), one a rack in each, racks about 1.6 m apart, ±0.3 in x and z from the overhead; the starboard racks 1.1-1.5 m further out and three groups 3-4 m further forward than before, two entries that were a deck-edge fitting and a hose station dropped. rows: small canisters (blue in the overhead), their heights not measured. domes_edge: centres, sizes and platforms from the overhead (±0.4); the second's floor, top and the foot of its bracket from dvids9142613; the others' floors at the catwalks' and their knees as the catwalks'; a fourth dome at x 0.5 added. catwalks: plans from the overhead (±0.3), the floor 16.9 (±0.4) between the racks' bottom and the fascia; the bow's knees 2.05 m apart, their feet 0.8 m below the floor (dvids9688116). Platforms off the port catwalk from the overhead; the widths of those at x 96-164 assumed. Provisional, not measured: the railing (1.0 m, posts every 1.5 m), the toe board (0.1 m), the nets (1.5 m out from the railing's top, rising 0.4 m, frames every 2.3 m as the overhead's sawtooth on the diagonal; the slope as ABS's helideck rule's) and where they run (the 2022 port view, the bow's in dvids9688116). Not built: the folded net frames at elevator 3.
notes.transom: references/research/transom: points triangulated in 2-4 photos through the catalogue's cameras, vertical edges by their rays flattened onto the horizontal plane, outlines cast from the dead-astern dvids7107228 onto the triangulated planes (its 3° lean removed). transom.face: the upper face at x -164.35 (±0.2; the opening's four edges in two photos each), from the walkway (7.0 ±0.3) to the deck; its opening's outline ±0.15, the corners' radii ±0.3, its back wall at -161.2 (±0.5, one life ring in three photos). windows: six, ±0.15. catwalk: the dark band under the deck's edge, railed. walkway: the opening's floor carried aft to x -167.2 (±0.5), its fascia and lower member from astern; railing 1.0 m, posts 1.8 m apart (rough). frame: eight black posts under the walkway's aft edge, its end posts as vertical edges (x ±0.4), into the water; the fenders on it by eye. drop: references/research/drop (drop_layout.py). plinth: the Phalanx's top at 9.2 (±0.4, two photos), its plan 3 x 3 m by eye. hull.transom.points: the lower transom's corners above the water (±0.15, port and starboard alike below 3.2); under water its run to the keel is not seen. The lower transom stands at -163.4 ±0.3 by its chocks, the hull's -163.0 within that. Not built: the raised platform inside the recess, the box starboard of the Phalanx, the doors and fittings, the deck edge's white band (round-down or paint, not resolved).
notes.deck2: references/research/deck2: dvids7694421 (2023-03) rectified through its solved camera (3.0 px), the primary source; noaa2022 re-registered (a mosaic seam from (45, -45) to (98, 22), the image forward of it 6.4 m to starboard); commons220325-CO784-2240 through its camera. The two images agree to about 0.4 m, the floor on a mark seen in one. markings: the existing ones checked (centreline within 0.01 m, yellow sections 0.25, bars 0.0-0.3, the 78 0.15); the edge stripes run to u 227.4, 224.4 (port) and 243.9, 246.9 (starboard), not 197.37 and about 232, which were the 2022 mosaic's seam; the slots 0.10 m wide, not 0.30. New: bars 0 and starboard 9, the foul lines and dashed lines, the catapults' foul lines, the elevators' red-and-white outlines, the deflectors' yellow outlines (on the panels, which wear the deck's texture), the weapons elevators' hatches, helicopter spots 2-6, the waist cross bars, the catapults' track bands, the deck-edge line and the bow's and quarter's lines; each with its photos and sigma in results.json. zone: the darker landing-area non-skid (±1 m, 2022). stains: the touchdown rubber, its shoulders, the rollout, the deflectors' spill (darkening in linear light, feathered). paint: the deck's non-skid (82, 84, 88), the yellow (210, 162, 62) and the red (150, 62, 62) from the 2025-2026 deck-level photos, scaled so their white is the table's (±15-25). lights.edge: the port row out to the longer stripes, 17 as the starboard's (the replica's), the rule's spacing. Not measured: the distance numerals, spot 1, the pendant supports' outlines, the tie-down grid, the deck after 2023-03.
notes.island2: references/research/island2: three in-era photos resected on the island's known points (2.5-8.6 px, leave-one-out 0.02-0.4 m) and the catalogue's cameras; parts cast onto the planes they stand on or triangulated, each with its sigma in results.json. island.details: the mast's faceted trunk (2.6 x 2.1 m, not the 4 m pole), its ring bands, middle platform and drum, the yardarms' railings, radars, loudspeakers, antenna clusters, braces and whips, the mast house's railing and antennas, the masthead's platform, antenna and whip, the gaff's railing; the body's walkways and railings, the starboard platform, log-periodic antennas, the aft dishes and the ladder. The yardarm's deck 45.95-46.65, the gaff 55.4-55.85 to x -101.5, the bridge windows 32.25-33.2 (the forward view, tilted, reads 32.2-33.9; still open). weapons: the Mk 29 (a fit on 14 corners in two photos, 4.9 px; no public dimensions), the Mk 49 RAM (navy.mil's working circle, the guide measured) and the Mk 15 Phalanx (navy.mil, FAS, GD-OTS; the radome measured) as parts, each mount stowed as photographed: the Mk 29s trained outboard, level (their tops 17.87 and 18.2, not 18.21 and 18.68, which were triangulated across two dates and two poses); the starboard aft RAM aft, on its guide's middle (1.2 m from the painted circle's centre); the port forward RAM's pose and side not seen, on a pedestal to the overhead's top; the Phalanxes' gun training not resolved, the fantail's on a 1.59 m pedestal. antennas: the bow mast square, 0.6 m, to 30.9, its cap, whip, lights, dish and radome (dvids9688116); the port whips' hinge housings 0.6 m by eye. Not measured: doors, vents, the floodlights' fixtures, the roof railings, the port whips' length, the masts on the port sponsons and bow platforms.
notes.knuckle: The carrier session's second pass (references/research/sides2/knuckle_layout.py): a metre grid cast through the level starboard beam's camera (dvids9167788) and the 2022 port view's (commons221126-QI061-2036R) on the hull side's plane, ±0.3 m. hull.knuckle: level at 4.6 on both sides from x -127 to 65, where the bow's rise begins; the starboard's steps under elevators 1 and 2 (5.7-5.9) were the blisters below them, its dips and wobbles (4.4-5.1) overhangs' shadows on the lit edge it was read from, and the loft ran each as a ramp, which read as a wavy line. hull.blisters: under elevator 1 (x -82.7 to -45.3, y 2.2-4.85) and elevator 2 (-4.5 to 30.5, 1.9-4.6) rounded at each end, under elevator 3 to port (-120.5 to -95.5, 2.3-5.3) a ribbed box with square ends; each stands out 1.0 m by eye (±0.5, its end face in the port view).
notes.tubs: tubs: the gun tubs on the aft sponsons' outboard faces (references/research/stern: plans ±0.4, floors 12.3 and 12.14, the knees' feet at 9.82 and 8.7), each a floor, a railing round its outboard sides (1.1 m, by eye) and a knee at its aft end; weapons.kinds.gun: the gun on each floor, a remotely operated mount with a sensor dome, about 2.6 m tall and its barrel 2.3 m, by eye with the crewman beside the port one (dvids7694418) and its type not named in a source found; trained forward as the port one is photographed (the starboard one's train not seen). The knees' holes are not built.
notes.front: hull.front: the stem's front below the face, its half-width rising from the forefoot's knife edge 2 m under the waterline (not seen) to the face's bottom edge (references/research/bow/front_layout.py): through the photo match's cameras, the head-on view's shadowed front (dvids3299641, ±0.5 m at y 1 to ±2.4 at 7, an upper reading) and the port edge seen 26.7° off the bow (dvids9688116, 0.72-2.09 at y 0.75-7.2), ±0.3 m above y 3 and ±0.4 below. Built flat, the sections ahead of the last station running straight to it, with a section at each knot of the stem it rises past.
notes.weathering: weathering: the paint's wear as photographed in 2022-2026 (decision 17, amended 2026-11-03), generated by weather.py and placed from the photos, never projected from them (references/research/weather/weather_layout.py): an atlas per group, its texels' occlusion baked from the geometry (within 3 m), plates and seams by rule (the island's bands 1.8 m from the deck, butts every 3 m; the hull's strakes 2.4 m from the waterline, butts every 9 m), tone 3% plate to plate with touch-ups in 7% of 1.3 m cells, streaks down from the windows' sills, the radar faces' lower edges, the details' undersides and the levels' lips (the island) or the sponsons' lower edges and the deck's edge (the hull), grime 2.5 m up from the deck or the boot top, walking surfaces darker. The island's streaks at 0.8 strength (0.5 read too faint beside dvids9135541's rust runs, compared close on the upper block's forward face).
notes.lettering_cutout: lettering.cutout: the lettering's atlas is clear but for the text and its outline, so each plate shows the weathered face behind it; lettering.colour 215, 216, 211, the 78s' off-white as photographed in 2024-2026 (references/research/island3: dvids9135541, 8200390), duller than the 236, 236, 230 the plain faces wore.
notes.island4: references/research/island4 (report.md, results.json): six cameras resected on the island's points (4.0-14.2 px), two close port photos mapped by plane homographies; parts cast onto the faces they stand on or triangulated (0.1-0.15 m unless the report says otherwise). The base's top and the overhang's soffit at 25.95 (cast 25.86-26.06 in two photos); the lower block's forward face one face leaning back 14 degrees (x -79.0 at the soffit to -80.2 at 30.8), the upper block's 15 degrees to its roof at 40.4 (radar_small_3's corners, the floods' rail, the capsule's foot); the bridge's face where its window posts stand (x -81.4 at z 33 to -81.75 at 20.6). Windows where the photos put them and the three bands they found; frames, mullions, wiper motors and head conduits as photographed; the PriFly glass's outward cant (0.15 m) not modelled, its glass on the face. The radomes turned to their measured profiles. The floods, the soffit's beams, the walkways' stiffeners and struts, the bridge wing's underside, the ladders, pipes and stair (its z from one view, +-1.5 m), the fittings on the base's faces (the aft face's heights from a camera reading 0.5-0.8 m low, +0.5), the halyards to their horn and post. No flags (the user, 2026-11-03). The crane aft of the island is a deck vehicle (task: deck vehicles), not built here. The 78s traced from dvids9493406 rectified on the port face (block numerals, a drop shadow 0.13 m right and 0.12 m down, lamps 0.47 m apart 0.11 m off the white, 33 round the 7 as counted, about 36 and 10 in each counter round the 8); both sides the same design, the starboard on the helper's middle (its camera read the digits 12% wider). Stencils and placards from their measured boxes; the port face's second S has no position and the starboard base's small stencil could not be read, so neither is drawn. Weathering: measured runs, each face's streaks scaled to its photos'; the radomes their own group, grey streaks below their widest seam.
notes.deckwear: references/research/deckwear: the user's photo of the Ford under way (2023, a repost without a credit, looked at only) for what to show; every number from public-domain photos rectified onto the deck through their photo-match cameras. paint.deck: the deck's non-skid as a share of the white and the yellow stripes in dvids7107230 and dvids7107228 (unclipped), 0.21-0.30 of the white in linear light; it was a provisional (82, 84, 88). The landing area the same paint (2022-2023 photos read it 0.7-1.5 of the deck by view and patch; noaa2022's darker coat was new). wear.tyres: the band in dvids7694421 (2023-03-19, near-nadir), its core and shoulders' shares along the landing line in measured; the generator's numbers fitted to it (rms 0.09 over 36 bins). wear.tyres.touchdown.round: the band's aft edge rounded, its aftmost on the centreline, the touchdowns the later the farther off it (the user, 2026-11-04, from the photo; rms 0.105 then). wear.deflectors: the panels' soot by its moments in the same photo, alike on all four (0.43-0.44 along from the aft edge, 0.50-0.57 across, spread 1.0 x 2.1 m, its core 0.83-0.93 dark), set at 0.25 along, nearer the aft ends (the user, 2026-11-04); their tan the ends' mean, 2.07, 1.56, 1.12 times the deck in linear light. wear.mottle: the plain non-skid's spread there, 0.07 over 8 m squares. wear.spots: fluid drips by rule, as many as the parking areas show, none in the landing area. weathering hull decks: the aft sponsons' tops, the stern's lower decks, tan non-skid measured at 1.74, 1.33, 0.95 times the deck (the mean of dvids7694421, 7694418 and 7107228, port and starboard), set halfway to the deck's grey (the user, 2026-11-04); dirtied by rule to port_aft's spread in dvids7694421 (0.15 over 2 m squares, 0.11 over 4 m).
notes.deckwear2: references/research/deckwear (deckwear2_layout.py, scripts, data), dvids7694421 rectified onto the deck. The parking areas as the rest of the deck: the photo's blotchier, stained parking areas looked worse (the user, 2026-11-04). wear.tiedowns: rows 1.563 m apart fore and aft, a fitting every 2.42 m, alternate rows half a step on, the phase holding over 100 m; none on the track covers or the deflectors; 0.22 m across in the photo, drawn 0.14 m and fainter (the user, 2026-11-04). wear.deflectors.forward: the scorch forward of each hinge, 0.3-0.6 dark in its first 2 m within about 3 m of the track, in place of the rectangles stains.*_deflector_spill. wear.taxi: by rule, faint (the user, 2026-11-04). The track covers 1.15 times the deck and their middle 1.22 (catapult 1's profile across, 18 stations; the others under parked aircraft). The red-and-white lines' dashes a faded orange (175, 132, 105), their cores against the deck (the yellow line's measured the same way within 3-20 of its paint). The stern's lower decks a quarter of the way to the measured tan, less dirty (the user, 2026-11-04).
notes.wear: references/research/weather (wear_layout.py, scripts): the wear by zone, 0 almost clean to 1 the most worn, from public-domain broadsides, transoms and bows laid over the model through their photo-match cameras and measured inside each face against its own level. The hull's lower walls 1 (5.4-7.3% spread over 2 m, 2.2-3.8% over 0.5 m in 2022-2025), the transom 0.8 (8-14%), the undersides 0.75, the sponsons' sides and the flare 0.45 (3.6-4.5%), the bow's upper flare 0.3; the island 0.35, its lowest storeys 0.6, its top 0.2 and the mast 0.12 (3.3% and 1-2% over 0.5 m); the radomes 0.1, the Phalanx's plain; the boot top its own colour atlas, scuffed at the bow and quarters. The effects at full wear fitted on flat walls to the lower hull's spreads (the user, 2026-11-04: slightly worn and very slightly dirty, to match the deck).
notes.transom2: references/research/transom2 (transom2_layout.py, scripts, data): DVIDS 7694418 (2023-03-19, the user's photo reposted), pixels cast through its camera onto the transom round's planes or the model. transom.details: the recess's mezzanine with its railing and ladder, the back wall's two tall doors, the cabinet, two red lamps and the life ring; the walkway's white cabinet and its fascia's two fittings; the ladder up the drop bar; the two scupper outlets and the pipe on the face; the lower transom's mooring chocks and a smaller round fitting (port only seen); the boat landing (a slatted deck at y 0.5 with railings, braces and a ladder); the port quarter's two round chocks; the back wall's door assembly 3.1 x 5.4 m and the locker beside it (they read too small, the user). deck.round: the round-down, 0.63 m over the last 2.9 m to the aft edge (the transom round's profile). Windows rounded and framed; nine side windows at z -33.3. The round-down's nets on the deck's aft edge. markings.ramp white from z -5.0 (two photos within 0.03 m), ramp_port light grey 0.66 of it (the bands in 7694418 are shadows). markings.centreline: the centreline and its first yellow section carried to the aft edge and drawn over the ramp (its yellow runs on across the round-down in 7694418, the user); transom.details centreline_fascia: the yellow down the edge plate to 16.96. weathering hull runs: the rust under the scuppers and down the lower transom as photographed. port_aft deck seams 2.84 x 1.27 m.
notes.island5: references/research/island5 (island5_layout.py), DVIDS 7694418 cast through its camera. island.cabs: the four glazed levels seen through, each a room cut from a metre under its sill to its head and an opening through each glazed face: the flight control (35.38-36.51; port from x -83.56 aft to the corner, round the aft face to z 22.3, forward), the bridge (32.6-33.45; port from -82.76 to -96.6, forward, starboard wing), level three (30.08-31.11; port from -83.32, round to 22.0) and level two (27.29-28.52; port from -84.96, round to 22.4), as cast in DVIDS 7694418 and commons170728-ES536-0113 (within 0.12 m), each head under the walkway above it; panes leaning out 0.25 m at the head, mullions every 1.5 m, a wiper per bay. The windows those levels' panes replace keep their sills at the photo's heights; island4's frames for them dropped. The port walkways' floors as cast in both: the bridge's 31.46 and level three's 28.87 (island2 had 30.8 and 28.45), the bridge's forward walkway with the port one at 31.46 (DVIDS 9688116 casts it 31.15-31.47), the flight control's 33.8 as it was; they run aft to the corner and round it with their bands, solid panels filling their railings; a strut whose foot would stand in a cab's glass dropped. The aft-port corner (a helper's triangulation in DVIDS 7694418, 7107229, 7489972, 9690464, 7464762 and commons170728-ES536-0113): radar_large_2 on a face of its own facing 122 degrees and leaning back 15, 4.05 m wide with a 0.18 m frame and a pillowed cover, on a housing (radar_housing, y 28.9-35.0) whose face meets the port side and the aft face outboard of ours, the aft tower's and level three's corners cut back inside it (level three split at 28.9); the upper block's aft-port corner on radar_small_1's face (122.7 degrees, leaning back 10.5; ours was 153), with a row of 14 floodlights along it at y 40.65 in a recess (to 41.17) under a fascia to 41.69, a parapet along that edge. The radomes turned to profiles fitted through the solved cameras in ten photos (scratchpad domes/results.json, rms 1.4-2.5 px): roof_aft bowing out to 1.95 at 42.92, the caps narrower than island4's, roof_forward 0.53 m aft. Halyards as cast in DVIDS 7694418: 14 to starboard (six to island4's horn, eight to a flag bag on the bridge wing's roof) and 8 to port (to a small railed platform above the flight control's roof, +-1.5 m); four port lines whose lower ends no photo resolves are left out. Second pass (the user's photo, a repost, looked at only; DVIDS 7489972 through island2's camera less the 95 px it reads aft, and 7694418): the port glass ends at x -88.6 and each glazed level turns the corner on a chamfer to (-92.0, 22.3), the blocks with it; open railings (solid panels hid the windows) following the chamfer; aft of it solid ledges to z 22.1 with angled ends, stopping at the array's housing; the rooms dark, a frame every 2 m, wipers on the forward faces only; eight more floodlights along the flight control roof's port edge; the port "S" on the bridge's ledge. Third pass (the user, DVIDS 9405715: the lettering sits otherwise against the ledges): the base's port lettering as 9405715 lays it out along the face (a projective map through the base's forward corner, the port ladder and the aft edge, the warning's lines reading 5.77 and 6.56 m against 5.7 and 6.4): the warning from -94.34, the aft CO2/PKP pair and AFFF 15C 1.3-1.4 m aft, the forward placards within 0.45 m, the awards from -96.05 at 27.9-28.4 and 26.5-27.1; the level-two ledge ending at -95.2 +- 0.4, short of the awards (2017's and 2022's cameras put it at -97.1, but read this face 0.5-1.0 m off), the ledges above ending at the array's housing.
notes.transom3: references/research/transom3 (transom3_layout.py, scripts): DVIDS 7694418 with 7107228 and 9142598, pixels cast through their cameras onto the layout's planes, each checked against something on it. sponsons.fantail: its underside sloping from the fascia's foot (6.2) to the lower transom (3.4), its starboard edge out to the box's; transom.plinth: the Phalanx's gun deck raised to 8.49 with sloping sides; transom.details stern3_*: the box behind the mount (top 12.6, z 15.3-20.5, 1.05 m out, +-0.5), the fantail's railing, fairlead and gas bottles, the LSO's windscreen with its two windows at the port quarter's corner, the box on its pedestal on the sponson's deck, a hose reel on the gallery, the red ladder down to the stern's catwalk. sponsons.quarter_starboard: the transom face run on to the starboard_aft sponson's corner down to 9.9. catwalks: the port quarter's gallery with its net; nets sagging 0.2 m between frames. The starboard_aft sponson's aft-face bottom left as marked (10.29-9.34): 7694418 and 7107228 show a silhouette 0.3-1.3 m lower but sloping opposite ways, so likely the hull beyond. The dark netted space by the sponson's forward end in 7694418 casts onto no surface the model has, so is not built.
notes.overhead: references/research/overhead (overhead_layout.py, scripts): DVIDS 7694421 (the 2023 overhead), pixels cast through its camera onto the deck or a sponson's top, each checked against something known beside it; the colours kept as they were (the user). markings overhead_*: the barricade stanchions' trays outlined in orange with their small marks, an orange rectangle and square and a white double square at the bow. transom.details overhead_*: the starboard aft sponson's white grid (0.596 x 0.673 m) and the red circle round the RAM; the port aft sponson's pipe, low box and the netted cage at its forward end (posts and height from 7694418), and the gallery's ladder down to it. catwalks: the port gallery ends at the cage (x -143). Left out: the Mk 29's shadow (it read as a hatch), the loose hose and planks.
notes.iccs: references/research/iccs (iccs_layout.py): the plans cast through DVIDS 7694421's camera; the bow's rise through 7107230's and 7107228's; the bow's body from a copyrighted Business Insider photo (measured only, decision 28) with DVIDS 8755444 and 9425021: faces leaning in, 0.15 m inside the lid at the foot and 0.45 at the head, a pane in each; the waist's from DVIDS 9259190: two panes inboard and one in each angled face, a thin lid, its lean not measured, its outboard face and what it stands on not seen.
notes.drop: references/research/drop (drop_layout.py): the drop-light pole's yellow found across its axis every 0.2 m in DVIDS 7107228, 7694418, 9142598 and 7107229. It stands at x -165.3 z 7.45 (fitted to three photos at 3.6 px), 0.4 m wide, from 16.4 (no yellow from the edge plate down to 16.25-16.5 in all four) to 2.2 (2.1-2.3), in two sections with nothing from 11.65 down to 9.0 (three photos; the box beside the gap is 1.1 m forward of the pole, at the mezzanine's edge, so it hides nothing). The walkway is cut back round it to a ledge at x -165.1 from z 5.9 to 7.9 (+-0.3), as the pole shows unbroken through the walkway's height dead astern and from the port quarter; its railing turns in along the cut. The ladder up its port side runs on down to its foot. Its lamps belong to the lights.
